Issued at 302 AM CDT Mon Oct 26 2026

Early this morning water vapor satellite imagery along with upper 
air analysis showed an upper trough extending from WY, south- 
southeast into eastern NM. An upper low was moving onshore across 
across the Pacific Northwest. An upper ridge was centered across the
western Gulf and extended northward into the mid MS River Valley.

The 6Z surface map showed a surface front extending from northern 
MI, west-southwest across southern IA, then west-southwest across 
southeast NE into north central and northwest KS. A line of 
scattered rain showers extended north of the front across southeast 
NE, southwest into north central KS. Temperatures north of the front 
were in the mid 40s to lower 50s. South of the front, across the CWA,
temperatures were in the upper 50s to mid 60s.

Today through Tuesday:

The surface front across north central KS/southeast NE will remain 
nearly stationary Today. Most CAMs show the showers across north 
central KS early this morning will diminish by mid morning across 
north central KS. As the H5 trough across CO and eastern NM lifts 
northeast across western KS later Today, then into eastern NE and IA 
Tonight into early Tuesday, the ascent ahead of the H5 trough will 
allow showers to redevelop across north central KS, and these showers
will then move east through the night across northeast and east 
central KS. Most CAMs show 50-100 J/KG of MUCAPE Tonight through 
Tuesday, so don't be surprised if you hear an occasional clap of 
thunder. The front will push southeast into the central counties of 
the CWA, before becoming stationary. The scattered to numerous 
showers should diminish through Tuesday afternoon as the H5 trough 
lifts farther northeast across western IA, shifting the ascent across
north central MO and central IA. The RAP/NAM/GFS show frontolysis 
occurring late Tuesday afternoon through Tuesday night. The upper low
over the Pacific northwest will shear apart into separate H5 
troughs. The lead H5 trough will lift northeast across the northern 
Plains. The second H5 trough will dig slightly southeast across 
WA/OR.

Tuesday night through Friday:

Wednesday looks dry. Wednesday night into Thursday, the secondary H5 
trough across WA/OR will shift east across the northern Plains. This 
H5 trough may be a bit more amplified with the southern edge of the 
H5 trough axis moving east across NE/northern KS, providing stronger
ascent across northeast KS Wednesday night into Thursday. A surface 
cold front will also push southeast across northeast and east central
KS late Wednesday night into Thursday. The ECMWF and GFS are in good
agreement with a back building line of storms across eastern KS on 
Thursday. The ECMWF is quicker moving the front and H5 trough across 
the Plains. The GFS is slower and keeps the front nearly stationary 
across east central and northeast KS. The effective shear will be 
stronger and southerly 850mb winds will advect richer moisture 
northeast, ahead of the front. There will be a better chance for 
thunderstorms on Thursday, and there may be a few organized updrafts,
especially if the GFS solution is more accurate. 

The extended range models show a southern stream H5 trough across 
west TX lifting northeast under an amplifying H5 ridge axis across 
the mid and upper MS River Valley. Showers and thunderstorm chances
(45-65%) will increase Friday into Friday night. The effective shear
will be weaker Friday, thus I do not expect any organized updrafts. 
Highs will be in the upper 70s to around 80 degree. A slight cool 
down on Friday with mostly cloudy skies and periods of showers and 
thunderstorms. Highs on Friday will reach the lower to mid 70s.

Friday night through Monday:

The extended range models show a longer wave-length H5 trough 
developing across the western US. The southwest flow across the 
central and southern high Plains will cause a lee surface trough to 
deepen. Southerly surface winds east of the lee surface trough will 
allow richer Gulf moisture to advect northward. Any mid level 
perturbation ejecting northeast across the Plains will provide ascent 
for chance of showers and thunderstorms. Southerly winds will keep 
highs in the 70s into early November.
